name: sticky-gallery
title: Sticky Gallery
description: Architecture photos fill three equal columns on dark ground, and the centre column is held in place while the outer two keep sliding past. A large heading at the top explains the sticky trick.
use: A gallery wants a still focal column while the outer images keep moving past it.
avoid: Every photo has empty alt text, rows are fixed at 384 px, and thirteen large pictures load up front.
a11y: All photos use empty alt text, so the grid says nothing to screen readers, and smooth scrolling ignores reduced-motion. (keyboard: n-a, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Three equal columns of square building photos separated by thin dark gaps, with a white sculpture, an orange block and a glass tower in the middle column. Above them a big white heading sits on a faint dark grid.
behaves: Scrolling moves the left and right photo columns upward while the centre column stays fixed at the top, so fresh side pictures keep arriving beside the same three stills. The whole grid departs once the section ends.
customise: No props: the thirteen photo links are written one figure at a time in the file, and the column spans, fixed heights and heading copy are classes.
weight: moderate: Thirteen remote photos load at once; the pinning itself is plain CSS.
